title: The opacity alibi: before calling an AI result incomprehensible, test the test
standfirst: “Beyond human understanding” is a claim about minds, and it needs evidence about minds. A huge file, an unfair question or one failed lesson can each look like a human limit without being one.
summary: Three small examples, a padded program, a misleading explanation and an unanswerable question, show how tests can fake human limits, and what a fair test of understanding would need.
claimBoundary: Commentary and synthesis. The switch and light examples are constructed illustrations whose counts come from simple exact computer checks, not observations of people. The proposed experiments have not been run; no human study, frontier-model evaluation, demonstrated advantage over ordinary review or limit on human understanding is reported. Not externally peer reviewed or formally verified.

banner.alt: For three switches, a compact parity program takes 2 exclusive-or steps and a padded version takes 46. A table of all 8 switch settings shows both programs give identical outputs.
banner.caption: Constructed example, not experimental data. Step counts describe one literal way of evaluating each program, not human effort or the shortest possible explanation; the padded code is an illustrative excerpt.
